title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-13
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 바이어 선적 박스 파손 건 확인서·답변·새 부킹 확인 후 점심 전 법인장 보고, 이전가격 보고서 서명·송부, 금요일 정기 보고와 보험 재견적 회신.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Friday, November thirteenth. This is your English briefing for Friday.

Yesterday was a busy day. A shipment for the buyer had a problem with some wet cartons. You gave the final go-ahead on the transfer pricing report. You sent the new fire insurance quote to my director. You also sent the contract list to a head office manager. Today is the last working day before the health check on Saturday. Let's get ready together.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. The buyer's shipment with some wet cartons.

What is it? On Wednesday afternoon, our truck arrived at the warehouse in the south. The warehouse found some wet cartons, with the tape coming off. But we only heard about it on Thursday morning. The export-import manager asked the warehouse to hold the container until today. The warehouse said no. The cut-off was too close. So they took our shipment out of the container and loaded the other cargo.

Why is it important? Our shipment may now miss this week's vessel. The ship leaves on November eighteenth. If we miss it, there may be a delay cost, a new booking, or even air freight. The buyer may also make a claim. The export-import manager asked the trucking company to answer by five o'clock yesterday. She asked them to say when they first knew, and to confirm they will pay all costs. She also asked for a signed and stamped letter by today.

Your first action today. Check if the trucking company replied and sent the signed letter. Then check the export-import manager's answers to your questions. Find out the new booking plan with the buyer's agent. After that, give my director a short report with the facts, the cost risk, and the next step.
Number two. The transfer pricing report for signature.

What is it? The tax consultant sent the updated Local File on Wednesday evening. A Local File is the transfer pricing report we must keep for the tax office. The tax consultant fixed one section. For one comparable company, the tax consultant advised not to add a reason, and you agreed. Yesterday morning, you told the chief accountant to go ahead with this final version. You asked her to prepare the report book for my director's signature.

Why is it important? The deadline is today, November thirteenth. If it is late, we may have a problem in a tax audit. My director also said we must watch the margin, and keep it at a safe level this year.

Your first action today. Ask the chief accountant if the report book is ready. Bring it to my director for his signature in the morning. Then make sure the chief accountant sends the signed copy back to the tax consultant today.
Number three. The Friday reports and the fire insurance.

What is it? Every Friday, you send the weekly cash report to a head office manager at head office. You also send the weekly outsourcing report to my director. Yesterday afternoon, you also sent the new fire insurance quote to my director. This time, the machines keep the same basis as the current contract. The new premium is a little lower than the current one.

Why is it important? The weekly reports are routine, but head office notices when they are late. For the insurance, head office must report to the CEO one month before the policy ends. The head office manager is waiting for our answer.

Your first action today. Check my director's reply on the insurance. If he says okay, forward the quote to the head office manager with a short summary. Then prepare the cash report and the outsourcing report before four o'clock.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the export-import manager. You asked her questions about the wet cartons. Were the cartons loaded or still at the warehouse? Did anyone check the garments inside? Did she send the loading re-confirmation, and who approved it? Did the buyer's agent know? Please collect her full answer this morning. Here is a sentence you can use.
"Excuse me, could you let me know where the wet carton case stands now?"

Second, The warehouse leader. She said she would finish the rack work on November twenty-first. You said this is too late, and you split it into two parts. The finished-style rack must be done by Saturday, November fourteenth. For the interlining, she must tell you the number of rolls by today. Then she must upload them by next Wednesday. Here is a sentence.
"Excuse me, please tell me how many interlining rolls you have by the end of today."

Third, the data collection for customs and production. All team leaders must upload their latest forms to the shared folder by Saturday. On Wednesday, only one new file was added. Most teams only opened and saved old files. Please check the folders again today, and remind the teams that are slow. Here is a sentence.
"Please upload the latest version of each form by tomorrow, so that we can send everything to my director."

Fourth, the purchasing staff. She owes you the extra information for the sample room air conditioner. She also owes the whiteboard quote, and the electricity VAT invoices. VAT means value added tax. Many of these are already late. Here is a sentence.
"Excuse me, these three items are overdue. If you cannot finish them today, please tell me the reason and the date you can finish."

Fifth, the IT staff. Yesterday, you told him to use the retail version of Windows for the new PC. You asked him to update the purchase request with the PC and Windows together. Please check that the new purchase request is in the system. Here is a sentence.
"Excuse me, please make sure the PR shows both the PC and the Windows license."
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, the pattern manager. Yesterday at four thirty, the pattern manager sent you the dummy list for review. Dummies are the dress forms in the sample room. He is asking you to check the list. Your reply can start like this.
"Thank you, the pattern manager. I will review the dummy list and tell you which ones need a new cover."

Second, the accountant. Yesterday, the accountant sent you the October income statement. You need this for the monthly result report to my director. Please open it, check the main lines against last month, and send any questions. Your reply can start like this.
"Thank you, the accountant. I checked the October income statement, and I have a few questions."

Third, the head office manager at head office. The head office manager is waiting for the new fire insurance quote with the old machine basis. After my director says okay, reply with the two options, six months and one year. Your reply can start like this.
"Dear the head office manager, as you suggested, we kept the same basis for machines as the current contract."

Fourth, the compliance officer. Yesterday, she asked to sign a yearly maintenance contract for the fire system. You already replied. You asked for three new quotes under the same conditions by November nineteenth. So there is nothing more to do today. Just wait for her quotes.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Friday. The transfer pricing report must be signed and sent. The weekly cash report goes to a head office manager. The outsourcing report goes to my director. At five thirty in the evening, there is a team dinner for the merchandising and export-import teams.

Tomorrow, Saturday, November fourteenth. It is the health check day for all workers, all day. The compliance officer is in charge. Also tomorrow, the customs and production data is due from all teams. The warehouse leader's finished-style rack is due. The quotes for the electrical safety electrical checks and the CCTV hard disks are also due. And a foreign manager should return the residence card and the room key.
Sunday, November fifteenth, is the deadline for the contract list. You already sent it to a head office manager yesterday, so that one is done.
Part five. English review.
Let's review some expressions from this week. We will look at expressions from yesterday, two days ago, four days ago, and last week.

The expression is "Could you let me know where something stands?" It means, please tell me how far something has gone. For example, "Could you let me know where the interlining upload stands?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Could you let me know where the interlining upload stands?

The expression is "Please make sure that ... Otherwise, ..." It means, check this carefully, or something bad will happen. For example, "Please make sure that the mainboard is the right version. Otherwise, the RAM will not fit." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please make sure that the mainboard is the right version. Otherwise, the RAM will not fit.
The expression is "incorporate." It means to add changes or comments into a document. For example, "The consultant sent the updated report, incorporating our two changes." Now say it with me.
One more time. The consultant sent the updated report, incorporating our two changes.

The expression is "What would you suggest we do if ...?" It means, what is your advice in this case? For example, "What would you suggest we do if a new sewer is below the target grade after three days?" Now say it with me.
One more time. What would you suggest we do if a new sewer is below the target grade after three days?

The expression is "Please confirm with someone whether ..." It means, ask that person and check yes or no. For example, "Please confirm with the trucking company whether they will go back to the old price." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please confirm with the trucking company whether they will go back to the old price.
The expression is "on hand." It means what we have now. For example, "Before buying, please check how many mops the department has on hand." Now say it with me.
One more time. Before buying, please check how many mops the department has on hand.
The expression is "pending." It means until something is decided. For example, "Pending our decision, please do not wash the dummies." Now say it with me.
One more time. Pending our decision, please do not wash the dummies.

The expression is "For your reference, here is how we ..." It means, this is how we did it before, as an example. For example, "For your reference, here is how we sold the hanger lines in April." Now say it with me.
One more time. For your reference, here is how we sold the hanger lines in April.

The expression is "Payment will be made only once ..." It means we will pay only after something is done. For example, "Payment will be made only once the trucking company sends the signed letter." Now say it with me.
One more time. Payment will be made only once the trucking company sends the signed letter.
The expression is "notify." It means to tell someone officially. For example, "Please notify the buyer's agent about the delay today." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please notify the buyer's agent about the delay today.
Part six. Role-play.
Here is a short talk. Anthony reports the wet carton case to my director in the morning. Listen carefully.
My director: Anthony, what happened with the buyer's shipment yesterday?
Anthony: Good morning, my director. Some cartons got wet on the truck. The warehouse found them on Wednesday afternoon.
My director: Wednesday? Why did we only hear about it on Thursday?
Anthony: The trucking company did not tell us in time. The export-import manager asked them when they first knew. We are waiting for their answer.
My director: Did the shipment go on the vessel?
Anthony: No. The warehouse could not hold the container. They took our cartons out and loaded the other cargo.
My director: So it will be late?
Anthony: It may miss this week's vessel. The export-import manager is working with the buyer's agent on a new booking today.
My director: Who will pay for this?
Anthony: We asked the trucking company to confirm they will pay all costs. We also asked for a signed and stamped letter by today.
My director: Good. Don't pay their next invoice until we get that letter.
Anthony: Understood. Payment will be made only once they send the signed letter.
My director: And the garments inside? Are they damaged?
Anthony: We don't know yet. I asked the export-import manager to check the garments and send photos. Pending the check, we will not ship those cartons.
My director: Okay. Please notify the buyer's agent today. I don't want the buyer to hear it from someone else.
Anthony: Yes. I will make sure the export-import manager sends the notice this morning. I will report back to you before lunch.
My director: Thank you, Anthony.
Part seven. Let's practice two key sentences from the role-play.
Sentence one. "Payment will be made only once they send the signed letter." Now say it with me.
One more time. Payment will be made only once they send the signed letter.
Sentence two. "Pending the check, we will not ship those cartons." Now say it with me.
One more time. Pending the check, we will not ship those cartons.
Now one bonus sentence, for your talk with the export-import manager. "Could you let me know where the new booking stands?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Could you let me know where the new booking stands?
Part eight. Closing.

Today has one main job. Get the facts and the signed letter on the wet cartons, and report to my director before lunch. Also get the transfer pricing report signed and sent today. After that, finish the Friday reports, and send the insurance quote to the head office manager when my director says okay.
It is Friday. Finish the urgent things in the morning, and enjoy the team dinner in the evening.
Have a good day, Anthony. See you on Monday.
